label: Luke 19:1
text: He entered and was passing through Jericho.

label: Luke 19:2
text: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

label: Luke 19:3
text: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.

label: Luke 19:4
text: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.

label: Luke 19:5
text:
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him,
“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”

label: Luke 19:6
text: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.

label: Luke 19:7
text: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”

label: Luke 19:8
text: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

label: Luke 19:9
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.

label: Luke 19:10
text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

label: Luke 19:11
text: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.

label: Luke 19:12
text:
He said therefore,
“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

label: Luke 19:13
text:
He called ten servants of his, and gave them ten mina coins,

and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’

label: Luke 19:14
text: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’

label: Luke 19:15
text: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.

label: Luke 19:16
text: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’

label: Luke 19:17
text: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’

label: Luke 19:18
text: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’

label: Luke 19:19
text: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’

label: Luke 19:20
text: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,

label: Luke 19:21
text: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’

label: Luke 19:22
text: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth will I judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down, and reaping that which I didn’t sow.

label: Luke 19:23
text: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’

label: Luke 19:24
text: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him, and give it to him who has the ten minas.’

label: Luke 19:25
text: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’

label: Luke 19:26
text: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.

label: Luke 19:27
text: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”

label: Luke 19:28
text: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

label: Luke 19:29
text: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,

label: Luke 19:30
text:
saying,
“Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon. Untie it, and bring it.

label: Luke 19:31
text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”

label: Luke 19:32
text: Those who were sent went away, and found things just as he had told them.

label: Luke 19:33
text: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”

label: Luke 19:34
text: They said, “The Lord needs it.”

label: Luke 19:35
text: They brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt, and set Jesus on them.

label: Luke 19:36
text: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.

label: Luke 19:37
text: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,

label: Luke 19:38
text:
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!
 Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”

label: Luke 19:39
text: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”

label: Luke 19:40
text:
He answered them,
“I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”

label: Luke 19:41
text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,

label: Luke 19:42
text:
saying,
“If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.

label: Luke 19:43
text: For the days will come on you, when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,

label: Luke 19:44
text: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”

label: Luke 19:45
text: He entered into the temple, and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,

label: Luke 19:46
text:
saying to them,
“It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’

but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”

label: Luke 19:47
text: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.

label: Luke 19:48
text: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.

label: Zacchaeus, chief tax collector at Jericho
Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector (architelones), rich, at Jericho; Jesus lodged at his house
statement: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector (architelones, over other tax collectors) and rich, was in Jericho; Jesus told him 'today I must stay at your house', stayed, and the crowd murmured that he had gone in to lodge with a sinner.

label: Jericho's balsam was a prized revenue crop
statement: The plain of Jericho produced balsam prized as the region's most precious crop, farmed as a revenue source (under Cleopatra and Herod, and later imperial property). This is the economic background the verse's 'he was rich' points to at Jericho, not a fact the verse states.

label: Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore-fig tree at Jericho
statement: Zacchaeus ran ahead and climbed into a sycamore-fig tree (sykomorea) at Jericho to see Jesus, who was to pass that way.

label: Restitution: half of goods to the poor, fourfold to the defrauded
statement: Zacchaeus declared that he gives half of his goods to the poor and restores fourfold anything wrongfully exacted - fourfold being the restitution scale of 2 Samuel 12:6 (and the law's fivefold ox/fourfold sheep of Exodus 22:1).

label: A nobleman went to a far country to receive a kingdom; his citizens sent an embassy against him
statement: In the parable, a nobleman travelled to a far country to receive a kingdom and return, gave his servants minas to trade, and his citizens sent an envoy after him saying 'We don't want this man to reign over us'; on return he rewarded the servants and had his enemies killed before him. Evidence attests the events the parable appears to assume (Archelaus's journey to Rome and the Jewish embassy against him), not that the parable was told.

label: The mina, a money sum of about 100 drachmae
statement: The nobleman gave each of ten servants one mina (Greek mna) to conduct business until his return; the mina is a weight/money sum, in the Greek system equal to 100 drachmae.

label: A colt tied, never ridden; its owners question the untying
statement: Two disciples sent into the opposite village found a colt tied, on which no man had ever sat; as they untied it its owners (despotai) asked why they were untying it, and they answered 'The Lord needs it'.

label: Cloaks on the colt and cloaks spread on the road
statement: They threw their cloaks on the colt and set Jesus on them, and as he went they spread their cloaks on the road (no branches are cut in Luke).

label: Acclamation at the descent of the Mount of Olives: 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord'
statement: At the descent of the Mount of Olives the whole multitude of disciples acclaimed 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!' (Psalm 118:26 with 'King').

label: He wept over Jerusalem and said enemies would throw up a barricade, encircle and level it
statement: Jesus wept over the city and said that the days would come when enemies would throw up a barricade (charax) against it, surround and hem it in on every side, and dash it and its children within it to the ground, not leaving one stone on another. The saying is recorded neutrally; evidence attests the siege of 70 CE it describes, not the saying.

label: He taught daily in the Temple; the leaders plotted but feared the people
statement: He was teaching daily in the Temple; the chief priests, the scribes and the leading men of the people sought to destroy him, but could not find what to do, for all the people hung on his words.
